_README: MASTER-SIDE GATE REPAIRS, declared so scripts/regate-sweep.py can re-qualify the open PRs
each repair already unblocked (issue #927). Adding a record here is a CLAIM, made in the same
reviewed diff as the fix, that a `gate` failure carrying these assertion signatures was caused
by the named defect and not by the PR under test.
repair_pr   the PR that landed the fix on master. Its merged_at and merge_commit_sha are
resolved at sweep time, so the record does not have to know its own merge SHA.
harness     the scripts/selftest-suite.txt entry whose self-test carried the assertion.
Validated against the manifest by the self-test: a typo sweeps nobody.
signatures  the assertion NAMES, exactly as the harness prints them after `FAIL `, up to
(not including) the `: <got> (want <want>)` tail. A candidate PR is swept only
when EVERY failure in its gate log matches one of these — a PR that also failed
on its own merits is refused and stays red.
why         why these signatures are attributable to this repair rather than to the PR.
A record goes inert REPAIR_LOOKBACK_HOURS after its PR merged. Records are kept afterwards as
the audit trail for what was swept and on what grounds; they cost nothing but a skipped row.

signatures: no `producer | early-exiting consumer` survives anywhere in scripts/*.sh (#879)
repairs.why: #888 added a SIGPIPE scanner over scripts/*.sh; the scanner's own definition line in worker-live.sh matched the pattern it searches for, so the assertion fired on every PR regardless of that PR's content (#910). #917 excludes the scanner's own file. The assertion therefore says nothing about the PR under test on any tree without #917, which is exactly what makes a failure carrying only this signature attributable to the repair. Measured: at its worst the registry ran 3 of 3 red and merged zero PRs in 58 minutes; 7 of 37 open PRs still carried this failure after #917 landed, and every one of the six re-qualified by hand went green on a moved head.
